bib.title: Textbooks Are All You Need II: phi-1.5 technical report

question: Can a 1.3B model trained mostly on synthetic textbook-like data reach common sense reasoning performance comparable to models several times larger?
hypothesis: Data quality (synthetic textbook-quality data) matters more than scale for capability in small LLMs.
contributions: phi-1.5, a 1.3B model trained on ~30B tokens of mostly synthetic data, open-sourced as a raw base model
phi-1.5-web and phi-1.5-web-only variants to probe the value of filtered web data
Benchmarks on common sense, language understanding, math and coding, plus a toxicity evaluation

method.summary: A 1.3B decoder Transformer (phi-1 architecture) trained from random init for 150B tokens on a mix of ~20B tokens of new synthetic textbook-like data (seeded with 20K topics) and phi-1's 7B-token data. Two web-data variants (phi-1.5-web-only, phi-1.5-web) use 95B tokens of filtered web data. Evaluated zero-shot (mostly) with LM-Eval Harness against open models.

results.claim: phi-1.5 (1.3B) scores 0.734 on WinoGrande zero-shot, above Llama2-7B (0.691).
results.setup: zero-shot, LM-Eval Harness, authors' own pipeline; phi-1.5 1.3B trained 150B tokens
results.table: Table 2, row phi-1.5 (1.3B), column WinoGrande; Llama2-7B row 0.691

results.claim: phi-1.5 trails Llama2-7B on MMLU (0.376 vs 0.453).
results.table: Table 3, row phi-1.5 (1.3B), column MMLU; Llama2-7B row 0.453

results.claim: phi-1.5 reaches 40.2 on GSM8K (via coding) vs Llama2-7B 14.6 and Llama-65B 50.9.
results.setup: zero-shot pass@1; 'via coding' (solves by writing code); phi-1.5-web 44.6

results.claim: phi-1.5 scores 34.1 HumanEval and 37.7 MBPP; the paper says it outperforms all existing models including Llama 65B on coding tasks, but Llama-65B's MBPP is also 37.7 (tie) and HumanEval 23.7.
results.table: Table 4, row phi-1.5, column HumanEval; Llama-65B 23.7, MBPP 37.7 both
results.note: Text says outperforms Llama 65B on coding tasks; MBPP is a tie at 37.7 per Table 4

results.claim: Training the 1.3B phi-1.5 took about 1.5K A100 GPU hours on 150B tokens, vs more than 80K hours for Llama-7B on 1T tokens.
results.table: Table 1, row phi-1.5 (1.3B), column Train time (GPU hrs.)
results.note: Llama-7B figure is from Table 1 as printed, source of figure not given

results.claim: phi-1.5 trains on a 30B-token dataset for 150B tokens total (about 5 epochs).
results.quote: build phi-1.5, a 1.3 billion parameter model trained on a dataset of 30 billion tokens
results.note: Sec 2.2 gives 7B (phi-1) + roughly 20B (new) = about 27B; epochs not stated, 5 is inferred from 150B/30B

results.claim: The new synthetic data is roughly 20B tokens seeded with 20K topics; the only non-synthetic part is 6B tokens of filtered code.

phi-1.5-web-only (filtered web only, about 15% of RefinedWeb) outperforms existing models of similar size on common sense, though results are mixed in Table 2 (e.g. WinoGrande 0.604 vs Falcon-rw-1.3B 0.607).
results.note: Claim 'outperforms all existing models of similar size' is not true on WinoGrande per Table 2 (0.604 vs Falcon-rw-1.3B 0.607)

results.claim: Web data helps reasoning: phi-1.5-web scores 41.4 HumanEval vs phi-1.5 34.1.
On 86 toxicity prompts phi-1.5 passed 47, failed 34, 4 did not understand; Llama2-7B and Falcon-7B failed on 54 and 50.
results.setup: manual grading of base-model completions, authors' own prompt set, one grader not stated
results.quote: Of the 86 prompts, phi-1.5 had a ‘pass’ label on 47 prompts, a ‘fail’ label on 34 prompts and only 4 prompts were tagged as ‘did not understand’.

limits: Synthetic data generation (generator model, prompts, topic list) is not disclosed and the dataset is not released
No contamination analysis; no seeds or variance; benchmark numbers from authors' own pipeline
Manual toxicity grading on 86 prompts, graders and protocol not described; counts sum to 85
Model has no instruction tuning; does not stop properly, hallucinates, may produce toxic or biased output (authors concede)
phi-1.5-web uses 300B training tokens (Table 1) so is not data-budget-matched with phi-1.5
Text claims it outperforms all models on coding incl. Llama 65B, but MBPP ties at 37.7
Examples shown are from a checkpoint that might differ from released weights
